body:
readManifestForest's entries array is ordered by anchor topology (anchored-to segment, anchored-to seq, own ULID) for DISPLAY purposes — deliberately not a causal/temporal order across independent segments (see packages/gate-manifest/lib/forest.mjs's own header comment on readManifestForest). Several P3-P6 gate consumers use array position (`.at(-1)`, `indexOf`, `slice`) over this array as if it were chronological, which breaks once a ticket's P5 evidence spans more than one manifest.d/ segment:

- packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs: latestP5Entry/latestP5Revision pick `.at(-1)` as 'the latest' P5 entry; p5CompletionIntegrityErrors and openP5FindingErrors use `slice`/`indexOf` to decide whether a dry-pass or a killed finding came 'before'/'after' a p5-complete entry.
- packages/runner/lib/acceptance.mjs: recordAcceptancePacket's latestP5Entry/latestP5Revision have the identical defect.
- packages/prosecute/lib/run.mjs: seedOpenFindingsFromManifest walks the forest in array order using sequential Map.set/delete to derive open findings; a finding raised in one segment and killed in a different segment can be processed out of causal order.

Concretely: if a finding is verified in one segment and later killed in a DIFFERENT, earlier-sorting segment (or vice versa), these consumers can report the wrong 'latest' P5 entry, misjudge whether a finding was killed before completion, or let P5 report clean with an unresolved finding.

This predates T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 3 (readManifestForest and its non-chronological ordering guarantee shipped in slice 1/2), but slice 3's segment writer is what first makes multi-segment evidence for a single ticket a live, reachable state — so this needs fixing before the forest is used in anger across P3-P6 gates.

Discovered and independently confirmed by 3 separate review passes during T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 3's development (adversarial-review + 2 of 5 P5 prosecution lenses): see PR #411 for full context and reproduction reasoning.

Acceptance criteria:
1. assertPhase (runner/lib/assertions.mjs), recordAcceptancePacket (runner/lib/acceptance.mjs), and seedOpenFindingsFromManifest (prosecute/lib/run.mjs) no longer rely on forest array position to determine chronology across segments. Either scope each read to root + the current branch's own open segment (mirroring the readOwnChains/peekOpenSegment pattern already used by tickets/lib/doctor.mjs, ticket-sync/lib/reassign.mjs, and ticket-sync/lib/push.mjs), or establish a genuine causal order (e.g. reject/ignore evidence from foreign segments) before doing any array-position-based reasoning. Verify: a new test with two lineages where segment creation order and evidence-append order diverge, proving the P5/P6 gates pick the causally-correct entry regardless of forest array position.
2. Existing runner and prosecute test suites stay green. Verify: node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs
3. No regression in the P5 dry-pass convergence semantics for the common (single-chain) case. Verify: node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs
title: Fix P5 finding-lifecycle logic that treats forest array order as chronological
